meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hi') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'знать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to recognise; to find out', paired with 'узнавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to find out, to learn') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'll find out where he is.
You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'about' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.text: Не волнуйся ты насчёт этого Мишкина.
examples.trans: Don't you worry about that Mishkin.

examples.text: Не волнуйся ты насчёт этого Мишкина. Работаем мы с ним.
examples.trans: Don't you worry about that Mishkin. We're working on him.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арок'). Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'present, gift' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is a present for you.

examples.text: Это семейный праздник. Как в детстве, с подарками!
examples.trans: It's a family holiday. Like when we were kids, with presents!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.en: to be liked, to make a good impression
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нравиться'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be liked', forming an aspectual pair with 'нравиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Синеозерск понравился в Москве больше других мест.
examples.trans: In Moscow they liked Sineozersk more than other places.
Don't be afraid, you'll like it.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('beautiful, handsome').

examples.trans: They have a very beautiful house.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'ring', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('ring, circle') (any round loop) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Watch. I'm taking off my ring.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
High-frequency Russian pronoun ('it') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А зачем? Я сам сделал так, чтобы он его написал.
examples.trans: And why would I? I'm the one who made him write it.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.
Secondary conversational sense ('what a lot of!') (in exclamations) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order
the infinitive 'Стоять!' as a police order

examples.text: То есть просто стоять и смотреть?
examples.trans: So we just stand and watch?

examples.text: Стоять на месте, никто не выходит из кухни без разрешения!
examples.trans: Freeze right there, nobody leaves the kitchen without permission!

считать.gloss: to count; to think, to consider

meanings.note: посчитать / сосчитать are the perfectives
Secondary conversational sense ('to consider, to believe') (я считаю, что... = I think that...) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'fine'.
Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'of course'.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: выбирать слова = to choose one's words

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('she') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Паша, я больше не хочу о ней слышать. Понял?
examples.trans: Pasha, I don't want to hear about her again. Understood?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'just'.
Secondary conversational sense ('easy') (это просто = it's easy) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.en: to send (something or someone to the speaker)
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'слать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to send (here)', paired with 'присылать'.

examples.trans: They sent me a free lawyer.

examples.text: Послушайте, здесь ошибка. Ко мне прислали бесплатного адвоката. В чём дело?
examples.trans: Listen, there's a mistake here. They sent me a free lawyer. What's going on?

meanings.note: Classical Greek compound borrowing ('фотография'), feminine noun. Common feminine noun meaning 'photograph, photo' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А можно с вами фотографию, пожалуйста?
examples.trans: May I take a photo with you, please?

examples.text: Давайте быстрее! А можно с вами фотографию, пожалуйста?
examples.trans: Hurry up! May I take a photo with you, please?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'арить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give (as a present)', paired with 'дарить'.

examples.text: А вы мне тоже айфон подарите?
examples.trans: Will you give me an iPhone too?

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'резать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'cut off, clip'.

examples.text: На перекрёстке его машину неожиданно подрезал чёрный джип.
examples.trans: At the intersection a black SUV unexpectedly cut off his car.

examples.text: Повар решил аккуратно подрезать края теста перед выпечкой.
examples.trans: The cook decided to neatly trim the edges of the dough before baking.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Secondary conversational sense ('tell me / tell us') (polite request) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to choose', forming an aspectual pair with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('something') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
colloquial, used as an adverb: что-то я не вижу = somehow I don't see it
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Secondary conversational sense ('different') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to buy', paired with 'покупать'.

examples.text: Юле бы дублёнку купили, Славику бы ноутбук.
examples.trans: We could have bought Yulia a sheepskin coat, and Slavik a laptop.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Secondary conversational sense ('to beg') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: общественный совет = public council
Secondary conversational sense ('piece of advice') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to call', forming an aspectual pair with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
